 Oral Judgment

1. This appeal has been preferred by the appellant - Insurance Company against the judgment and award dated 31.01.2022 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ahmedabad (Mirzapur) in MACP No.370 of 2017.
2. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties.

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are that on 12.12.2016, the deceased was travelling as a cleaner in a Bolero Pickup.

When the said Bolero Pickup reached the place of the accident, the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4758/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined driver of the vehicle drove it in a rash and negligent manner, as a result of which the vehicle turned turtle, causing the accident.
Due to the said accident, the deceased sustained fatal injuries and subsequently succumbed to the same.

4. Learned advocate for the appellant submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle, i.e.,
opponent No.1, was not holding a valid driving licence at the time of the accident and therefore the insurance company is required to be exonerated from its liability.
It is further submitted that the deceased was travelling in the Bolero Pickup as an unauthorized passenger, and the risk of such passenger is not covered under the terms of the insurance policy.
Hence, it is requested that the present appeal be allowed.

5. On the contrary, the learned advocate appearing for the respondent has strongly opposed the appeal and submitted that the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded just and proper compensation in view of the evidence available on record.
It was contended that the learned Tribunal has not committed any error in appreciating the evidence and determining negligence.
Accordingly, it was prayed that the appeal be dismissed.

6. Having heard the learned advocates for the respective parties and upon perusal of the record, it appears that the present appeal has been filed only on the ground of liability, and therefore the same is required to be decided within a narrow compass.

It also emerges that the learned Tribunal has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4758/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined appreciated the evidence in light of the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bimla Devi v. H.R.T.C., AIR 2009 SC 2819 and Parmeshwari Devi v. Amir Chand, (2011) 11 SCC 635.
7.

sentences.text: It appears from the record that the claimants have produced documentary evidence including the complaint at Exhibit-23, panchnama at Exhibit-24, and other relevant documents.
The involvement of the vehicle and the coverage of the insurance policy are not in dispute.
The appeal has been filed mainly on the ground that the learned Tribunal has committed an error in saddling the liability upon the insurance company and in passing an order of pay and recover.

8. After appreciating the evidence on record, the learned Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Bolero Pickup, which turned turtle after the driver lost control over the steering.

9. So far as the liability is concerned, the learned Tribunal recorded a finding that on the date of the accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence.

Despite service of notice, opponent No.1 neither appeared before the learned Tribunal nor produced any relevant document on record to rebut the contention of the insurance company regarding the absence of a valid driving licence.

Therefore, the learned Tribunal rightly drew an adverse inference against the driver of the offending vehicle in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu v. Vinod Kumar Lamba, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4758/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:

10.

sentences.text: In view of the above, This Court is of the considered view that the claimant is a third party, and merely because there is a breach of policy condition under Section 149(2)(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act, the third party cannot be denied compensation.

Such breach may give rise to a defence available to the insurance company against the insured, however the third party has nothing to do with such inter se dispute between the insurer and the insured.
In such circumstances, the Court may direct the insurer to pay the compensation amount to the claimant and thereafter recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

In this regard, reference may be made to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanjappan, (2004) 13 SCC 224, wherein it has been held that the insurer can be directed to first satisfy the award and thereafter recover the amount from the insured.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanjappan, (2004) 13 SCC 224
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said principle has also been reiterated in Pappu v. Vinod Kumar Lamba, (2018) 3 SCC 2008.

entities.text: Pappu v. Vinod Kumar Lamba, (2018) 3 SCC 2008
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned Tribunal has rightly passed the order of pay and recover.

11. In such circumstances, an order of pay and recover is required to be passed in order to protect the interest of the innocent third-party victim, which is the underlying object of the Motor Vehicles Act, being a social welfare legislation.
In this regard, reference may also be made to the decision of this Court in United Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Minor Sobhnaben Madhobhai

entities.text: United Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Minor Sobhnaben Madhobhai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL
CITATION
C/FA/4758/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined Patadiya, reported in 2026 (1) GLR 148, wherein it has been held that in such circumstances the Tribunal ought to pass an order of pay and recover.

12. Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that the learned Tribunal has not committed any error in directing the insurance company to pay the compensation amount and recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
13. In view of the above, the appeal being devoid of merits deserves to be dismissed.
Accordingly, the appeal stands dismissed.
If any amount is lying deposited before this Court, the same shall be transmitted to the learned Tribunal forthwith.
No order as to costs.
The Registry is directed to return the Record and Proceedings, if any, to the learned Tribunal forthwith.
(HASMUKH D. SUTHAR,J) ALI
